title: Alt-LIMS: Why Modern Labs Are Moving Beyond Traditional ELN and LIMS
summary: Discover how Scispot’s alt-ELN and alt-LIMS empower modern labs with automation, inventory management, and compliance-ready features, ensuring seamless lab data management and reproducibility.
body_markdown:
## TL;DR


- "Alt-LIMS" is Scispot's name for a connected, configurable alternative to rigid, standalone ELN and LIMS tools.
- Traditional systems often leave data split across notebooks, spreadsheets, and instrument PCs.
- An alt-LIMS links samples, experiments, inventory, and instrument data in one governed data layer.
- It suits fast-changing labs that need no-code changes, integrations, and AI-ready data.


See what a connected alt-LIMS looks like for your lab

Electronic lab notebooks and LIMS were meant to end paper, lost samples and copy-paste errors. For many labs they did half the job. The notebook holds the experiment, the LIMS holds the sample, the instrument PC holds the raw file and a spreadsheet holds everything in between. Scientists still spend hours stitching those pieces together. "[Alt-LIMS](https://www.scispot.com/lims) " and "[alt-ELN](https://www.scispot.com/elns) " are Scispot's terms for a different approach: keep the jobs ELN and LIMS do, but run them on one connected, configurable platform.


## **Why traditional ELN and LIMS fall short for modern labs**


The problem is rarely a missing feature. It is how the tools were built and bought:


- **Silos by design:** ELN and LIMS often come from different vendors with different data models, so linking an experiment to its samples is manual.
- **Rigid workflows:** changing a field or adding an assay can require vendor services or code, so labs work around the system in spreadsheets.
- **Instrument gaps:** results are typed or pasted in, which is slow and error-prone.
- **Data that is hard to reuse:** records are stored as pages and PDFs rather than structured data that analysis or AI tools can use.


If you are still deciding which tool you need, our guide on[choosing between an ELN and a LIMS](https://www.scispot.com/blog/how-to-decide-between-implementing-an-electronic-lab-notebook-eln-laboratory-information-management-system-lims) explains the classic split.


## **What an alt-LIMS and alt-ELN do differently**


- **One data layer:** samples, experiments, inventory, and results are linked records, so you can trace a result to its sample, protocol, and instrument run.
- **Reproducible protocols:** versioned, structured protocols make it easier for another scientist to repeat the work.
- **Inventory that keeps up:** stock levels update as work is recorded, with alerts before reagents run out.
- **Audit-ready records:** audit trails, version history, and e-signatures support your quality processes. Your lab still owns validation and SOPs.
- **Plain-English search:** scientists ask questions of their data instead of building reports.
- **Analysis-ready data:** structured outputs feed dashboards, pipelines, and machine learning without manual clean-up.


This is the same idea behind the[lab operating system](https://www.scispot.com/blog/laboratory-information-management-system) : ELN, LIMS, SDMS and QMS as apps on one platform rather than separate products to integrate.


## **Is your lab ready for an alt-LIMS?**


An alt-LIMS is most useful when several of these are true:


- Your assays, sample types or partners change every quarter.
- Scientists keep shadow spreadsheets because the current system is hard to change.
- Instrument data is still moved by USB stick, email or copy-paste.
- Leadership wants AI or analytics, but data is scattered and inconsistent.
- You are moving from a startup set-up to regulated or customer-facing work and need cleaner audit trails.


If your workflows are stable and one legacy LIMS already does the job well, a full platform move may not be worth it yet. Many labs start by connecting one workflow and expand once they see results.


### **How to evaluate an alt-LIMS**


Treat an alt-LIMS like any other lab system purchase and test it against your real work:


- Bring one live workflow to the demo: your sample types, your assay steps and your report, not a generic script.
- Ask a scientist, not an administrator, to change a field or add a step while you watch. If it needs a ticket, it is not configurable enough.
- List your instruments and check how each one sends data: direct integration, file parsing or manual upload.
- Ask how ELN records, samples and inventory link to each other, and whether you can trace a result back in a few clicks.
- Check exports and APIs so your data science team can use the data without screen-scraping.
- Ask for a phased rollout plan and a reference customer at a similar stage.


A good alt-LIMS vendor will be clear about what it does not do. Some labs keep a specialised instrument system, an ERP or a validated legacy QC tool and connect it, rather than replace everything at once. That is often the lower-risk path, and it lets scientists see value in weeks instead of waiting for a big-bang migration. The goal is fewer disconnected hand-offs, not a bigger system for its own sake.


## **What labs report after switching**


A[San Mateo molecular diagnostics startup](https://www.scispot.com/resources/how-a-san-mateo-based-diagnostics-startup-accelerated-operations-with-scispot-alt-lims) replaced a rigid legacy LIMS that needed coding for every workflow change. After moving to Scispot, the team reported 80% faster workflow adjustments, 50% fewer manual errors and 30% faster sample processing, driven by no-code configuration and direct instrument data capture.


Results like these depend on scope and adoption, but the pattern is common: most of the gain comes from removing manual hand-offs between tools, not from any single feature.
